parts.subtitle: Research shows that our olfactory sense is more influential than we realise
parts.article:
The Power of Smell
 
Research shows that our olfactory sense is more influential than we realise
 
A Dogs' noses are renowned for sensitivity to smells, while human noses are thought to be poor by comparison, yet that might be a misconception. According to recent studies, our noses are in fact acutely sensitive instruments that guide our everyday lives to a surprising extent. Subtle smells can change your mood, behaviour and the choices you make, often without you realising it. Our own odours, meanwhile, indicate emotional states such as fear or sadness to those around us. The big mystery is why we aren't more aware of our nasal activity. Noses have certainly never been at the forefront of sensory research, and were pushed aside until recently in favour of the seemingly more vital senses of vision and hearing. 'There has been a lot of prejudice that people are not that influenced by olfactory stimuli, especially compared to other mammals,' says Lilianne Mujica-Parodi, who studies the neurobiology of human stress at Stony Brook University in New York, in the United States.
 
B One of the first people to assert the relative unimportance of human smelling was Pierre Paul Broca, an influential 19th-century anatomist. After comparing the proportion of the brain devoted to smell in different animals, he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals, such as dogs, have a finely tuned sense of smell which they rely on to perceive the world, while we, along with other primates and the marine mammals, are microsmatic – we have small olfactory organs that we only rely on to a small extent. That idea seemed to fit with more recent studies which found that the majority of mammals have genes coding for about 1000 different types of smell receptor. Most of these genes aren't expressed in humans, giving our noses just 400 different types of receptor.
 
C Yet these findings may have been misleading. Brain scans now show that more of the brain is devoted to smell processing than Broca's anatomical studies suggested. And although we may have fewer types of receptor than other mammals, Charles Greer at Yale University in the United States has shown that the human nose and brain are unusually well connected, with each group of receptors linking to many more neural regions than is the case in other animals. That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents. Once researchers began looking, they found the nose to be far more sensitive than its reputation suggested. One study, for example, found that we can detect certain chemicals diluted in water to less than one part per billion. That means that a person can detect just a few drops of a strong smell like ethyl mercaptan in an Olympic-sized pool.
 
D 'We are also exceptionally gifted at telling smells apart, even in the case of two molecules whose only difference is that their structures are mirror images of one another. That is fantastic sensitivity,' says George Dodd, a perfumer and researcher at the olfaction group of the University of Warwick, in the United Kingdom. What's more, it's becoming clear that the brain's olfactory centres are intimately linked to its limbic system, which is involved in emotion, fear and memory. That suggests a link between smell and the way we think.
 
E The power of smell will be no news to estate agents, who often advocate the smell of baking bread or brewing coffee to promote the sale of a house. But there are more subtle and surprising effects too. When Hendrik Schifferstein and colleagues, from Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands, pumped the smell of orange, seawater or peppermint into a nightclub, the revellers danced more, rated their night as more enjoyable, and even thought the music was better than when there was no added scent. Meanwhile, Rob Holland, of the University of Utrecht in the Netherlands, found that the hint of aroma wafting out of a hidden bucket of citrus-scented cleaner was enough to persuade students in a hostel to clean up after themselves.
 
F Other work has found that scent can influence our cognitive skills. A study by William Overman and colleagues at the University of North Carolina in the United States found that when men were subjected to a novel smell – either good or bad – during a task used to test decision-making skills, they performed significantly worse than normal. The researchers conclude the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.
 
G Smells are especially good memory evokers, but it is actually a myth that odours trigger more detailed memories than other stimuli. 'The memory is not more accurate and you don't remember more details,' says Yaara Yeshurun at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, 'but it is unique in that it is more emotional.' This isn't surprising when you consider that there are certain brain areas dedicated to both emotion and olfaction, such as the amygdala, and there is a strong link between emotion and memory. In 2009, Yeshurun found that the link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is unpleasant rather than pleasant. She also discovered that the very first time we attach a smell to an object, it evokes a much greater response in our brains than for any subsequent encounter with the smell or object, laying down stronger foundations for the memory. That doesn't happen with any other sense. Since those first encounters with a smell would have happened at a young age, this explains why smells often transport us back to our childhood.

questions.question: a finding that humans can distinguish between two extremely similar substances

analyses.content: “Distinguish between two extremely similar substances” 对应原文的 “telling smells apart... two molecules whose only difference is... mirror images”。
(Paragraph D) “We are also exceptionally gifted at telling smells apart, even in the case of two molecules whose only difference is that their structures are mirror images of one another.”
题目提到人类可以区分两种极度相似物质的发现。原文D段开头引用George Dodd的话说，即使是两种唯一的区别在于结构互为镜像（mirror images）的分子，我们也有天赋把它们区分开（telling smells apart），选 D。

questions.question: a categorisation of species according to their sensitivity to smell

analyses.content: 题目提到根据对气味的敏感度对物种进行的分类。原文B段提到Broca建议哺乳动物可以被分为两大类（classed into two broad groups）：嗅觉敏锐的（macrosmatic）和嗅觉微弱的（microsmatic），选 B。
“Categorisation of species” 对应 “classed into two broad groups”。
(Paragraph B) “...he suggested that mammals can be classed into two broad groups: macrosmatic mammals... and... microsmatic...”

questions.question: an instance where smell negatively affected people's ability to make choices

analyses.content: 题目提到气味消极地影响人们做选择的能力的例子。原文F段提到Overman的研究发现，当男性暴露在某种新气味中时，他们在测试决策技能（decision-making skills）的任务中表现得比正常情况明显更差（significantly worse），选 F。
“Negatively affected... ability to make choices” 对应 “performed significantly worse... making their decisions emotional rather than rational”。
(Paragraph F) “...making their decisions emotional rather than rational.”

questions.question: a study that proved humans could perceive a tiny quantity of a substance

analyses.content: “Tiny quantity” 对应 “less than one part per billion / a few drops in an Olympic-sized pool”。
题目提到一项证明人类可以感知微量物质的研究。原文C段末尾提到一项研究发现我们可以检测到稀释到十亿分之一（less than one part per billion）的化学物质，甚至在奥林匹克泳池里的一两滴，选 C。
(Paragraph C) “One study, for example, found that we can detect certain chemicals diluted in water to less than one part per billion.”

questions.question: an observation that studies of the sense of smell have been undervalued

analyses.content: 题目提到关于嗅觉研究被低估的观察。原文A段提到鼻子从未处于感官研究的前沿（forefront），一直被搁置一旁（pushed aside），存在很多偏见（prejudice），选 A。
“Undervalued” 对应 “never been at the forefront / pushed aside / prejudice”。
(Paragraph A) “Noses have certainly never been at the forefront of sensory research...”

questions.question: an example of using smell to prompt people to buy something

analyses.content: 题目提到利用气味促使人们购买某物的例子。原文E段提到房产中介（estate agents）经常提倡用烤面包或煮咖啡的味道来促进房子的销售（promote the sale），选 E。
“Prompt people to buy” 对应 “promote the sale”。
(Paragraph E) “...advocate the smell of baking bread or brewing coffee to promote the sale of a house.”

questions.question: A faint smell could motivate people to do household chores.

analyses.content: (Paragraph E) “...Rob Holland... found that the hint of aroma... was enough to persuade students... to clean up after themselves.”
“Faint smell” 对应 “hint of aroma”；“household chores” 对应 “clean up”。
题目说微弱的气味可以激励人们做家务。原文E段末尾 Rob Holland 发现隐藏的清洁剂发出的一丝香气（hint of aroma）足以说服学生打扫卫生（clean up after themselves），选 E。

questions.question: Humans are better equipped to interpret smell than other species are.

analyses.content: 题目说人类比其他物种更有能力解读气味。原文C段 Charles Greer 表明人类鼻子和大脑连接异常紧密，连接的神经区域比其他动物多得多，这应该给我们很好的能力去处理（process/interpret）气味，选 C。
“Better equipped to interpret” 对应 “unusually well connected... good ability to process”。
(Paragraph C) “...Charles Greer... has shown that... That should give us a good ability to process incoming scents.”

questions.question: Smell is associated with feelings, rather than the logical part of the brain.

analyses.content: 题目说气味与感觉相关，而不是大脑的逻辑部分。原文F段 William Overman 的研究得出结论，气味刺激了与情绪相关的大脑区域，使决策变得情绪化而非理性（emotional rather than rational），选 F。
“Feelings... rather than logical” 对应 “emotional rather than rational”。
(Paragraph F) “The researchers conclude the scent stimulated brain areas connected with emotion, making their decisions emotional rather than rational.”

questions.question: Humans do not require a sophisticated ability to smell.

analyses.content: (Paragraph B) “One of the first people to assert the relative unimportance of human smelling was Pierre Paul Broca...”
题目说人类不需要复杂的嗅觉能力。原文B段 Pierre Paul Broca 认为人类是“microsmatic（嗅觉微弱的）”，我们只有很小的嗅觉器官且仅在很小程度上依赖它，这暗示了我们不需要像其他动物那样复杂的嗅觉生存能力，选 B。
“Do not require... sophisticated ability” 对应 Broca 提出的人类 “rely on to a small extent / relative unimportance”。

analyses.content: 题目说____是大脑中处理感觉和气味的一部分。原文G段提到有特定的大脑区域专门用于情感和嗅觉，例如“amygdala（杏仁核）”，填 amygdala。
“Part of the brain” 对应 “brain areas”，“feelings and smell” 对应 “emotion and olfaction”。
(Paragraph G) “...there are certain brain areas dedicated to both emotion and olfaction, such as the amygdala...”
题目说____气味与记忆建立特别强烈的联系。原文G段提到如果气味是“unpleasant（令人不快的）”而不是令人愉快的，记忆和气味之间的联系会更强（stronger），填 unpleasant。
“Especially powerful associations” 对应 “link... is stronger”。
(Paragraph G) “...Yeshurun found that the link between a memory and a smell is stronger if the smell is unpleasant rather than pleasant.”
题目说在所有感官中，气味有能力唤起对____的记忆。原文G段末尾说这解释了为什么气味经常把我们带回“childhood（童年）”，填 childhood。
“Prompt memories of” 对应 “transport us back to our...”。
(Paragraph G) “...this explains why smells often transport us back to our childhood.”
